summary: gcp-log-poc exfiltrates full environment to attacker GCP project at install and import time
details: gcp-log-poc 0.0.1 ships code in both setup.py and gcp_log_poc/__init__.py that decodes a base64-embedded Google Cloud service account credential (pypi-log-writer@nginxinc.iam.gserviceaccount.com, project_id 'nginxinc', a name that squats on NGINX, Inc.) and uses it to authenticate to Google Cloud Logging. The payload sent via _logger.log_struct contains dict(os.environ) in full, along with hostname, username, cwd, and OS details. setup.py executes this during `pip install` of the sdist, and __init__.py re-runs it on every `import gcp_log_poc`, so the exfiltration also fires from the installed wheel without any sdist build. On CI and developer machines, os.environ routinely contains credentials such as AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, NPM_TOKEN, and database passwords, all of which are transmitted to a destination controlled by the package author. The embedded base64 credential and the vendor-impersonating project name are deliberate concealment of the exfiltration channel.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
